salt extraction methods are more efficient in producing protein isolates from Vicia ervilia than the isoelectrophoretic sedimentation method.
the salt extraction method is more effective than isoelectric sediment method in producing V. ervilia isolates with high efficiency and purity.

the salt extraction (dialysis and miscellae) methods are more effective than the sedimentation at isoelectrical point (alkaline or acidic) in increasing the efficiency and purity of protein isolates of bitter vetch.

the development of protein isolates with high purity, protein rate and efficiency from the V. ervilial grain.
the production of protein isolate using different extraction methods and the results showed that the salt-dialysis and the miscella methods were more effective than isoelectric point methods.
the production of protein isolates from bitter vetch, which has not been previously studied.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the salt extraction method (salt-dialyzation and miscella) is more efficient than other methods in producing the V. ervilial protein isolates.
the protein isolates produced in this study are a good source of protein for the food industry.
the salt extraction method (salt-dialyse) is more effective in increasing protein efficiency, purity and content, and decreasing impurities and carbohydrate than the miscella extraction method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the salt extraction method (miscella) was the best method in producing V. ervilia isolates with high efficiency, high purity and protein content, and low impurities and carbohydrates.

the protein isolates produced from V. ervilia using dialysis and miscella sedimentations methods have a higher protein content, purity, and efficiency than the isolates produced using alkaline and acidic extraction-sedimentations at the isoelectrical points methods.

the V. ervilias protein isolate is a valuable source for the food industry and the production of isolates by salt extraction methods (dialysis-salt and miscella sediment) can be recommended for the production of protein isolates from V. ervilia.

the protein extraction method has a significant effect on the efficiency, purity, protein content and chemical compounds of V. ervilial isolates.
